title: Settings
welcome_title: Welcome! Three steps and you're done
welcome_1: Type your town in box 1 and pick it from the list.
welcome_2: Optional: paste the link of your calendar in box 5 (the help below the box shows where to find it).
welcome_3: Press Save at the bottom of the page. The mirror updates within a minute.
place_hint: Weather, sunrise and moon are calculated for this place.
place_help: Type the name of your town, press Search, then click the right line (the region tells look-alike names apart). Name, position and time zone fill in by themselves. If the search does not work, type the latitude and longitude yourself: on Google Maps or Apple Maps, press and hold on your home and the two numbers appear.
name: Name shown
no_result: No town found. Check the spelling, or try a bigger town nearby.
search_failed: The search needs internet. You can type the latitude and longitude instead.
region_hint: The country gives the public holidays, the first day of the week and the suggested news. Choosing a country also suggests its language.
region_help: Region only matters when some holidays exist in part of the country (for example Alsace-Moselle in France, or the German states). If you are not sure, leave “None”.
look_hint: Click the style you like: the preview on the right changes at once. “Auto” switches to the night colours after sunset.

calendar_hint: Beranda shows your appointments by reading a special link from your calendar. It can only read: it never changes anything. No password is needed, never type one here.
cal_where: Where do I find this link? (step by step)
cal_google: On a computer, open Google Calendar → gear ⚙ → Settings → on the left, click your calendar → “Integrate calendar” → copy “Secret address in iCal format”.
cal_apple: On icloud.com/calendar, click the ⓘ button next to the calendar → turn on “Public Calendar” → Copy.
cal_outlook: In Outlook on the web: ⚙ Settings → Calendar → Shared calendars → “Publish a calendar” → choose the calendar → Publish → copy the ICS link.
cal_nextcloud: In the Calendar app, open the calendar's menu → Share link → copy it. Beranda turns it into the right address by itself.
cal_proton: Paid Proton plans only: Settings → Calendars → your calendar → “Share with anyone” → Create link → Copy link.
cal_privacy: Anyone with this link can see your events, so keep it private. Beranda stores it only on your Raspberry Pi. If it ever leaks, you can make a new one from the same settings page (the old one stops working).
ics_placeholder: Paste the link here (https://… or webcal://…)
test_ok: It works: {n} events in the next 60 days. {next}
test_fail: This link does not work ({err}). Check that you copied all of it.
key_dates_hint: Births, remembrances, anniversaries: they get a mark on the calendar. With the year (2018-06-02) the screen shows how many years; without it (06-02) the date comes back every year.
label: Name
news_hint: One line at the bottom of the screen shows the latest headlines, one at a time. Titles only: no pictures, no ads, no account.
news_auto_hint: Beranda picks news about {city}, the main media of {country}, and an international medium in your language. Untick to choose yourself.
news_city_desc: Articles that mention your town, found by GDELT, a free open index of the world's press. Sometimes a title is off topic.
news_none_country: No preset media for this country yet. Pick international media, or add your own feed below.
news_custom_where: What is a feed, and where do I find one?
news_custom_hint: A feed (RSS or Atom) is a link that a news site publishes so that apps can read its latest titles. Look for the orange RSS logo or the word “RSS” or “feed” at the bottom of the site. Often it is the site's address followed by /rss or /feed. Paste it here and press Test.
photos_hint: A small photo frame on the main screen that changes picture every few seconds. You send the pictures from your phone or computer — there is no folder or path to type.
photos_folder: Folder path on the Raspberry Pi
photos_none: No photos yet. Tap “Add photos” above.
photos_empty: No photos found in that folder yet
photos_help: Tap “Add photos”: your phone or computer lets you choose pictures — from its gallery, and also from Google Photos, iCloud or Google Drive when those apps are installed (the picker lists them). Beranda keeps its own copy, shows the newest first, and ✕ removes a picture. Why no direct Google Photos or Google Drive link? Google does not allow small home apps to read a photo library, so choosing the pictures is the simple, reliable way. Dropbox does allow shared-folder links, so Beranda can follow one on its own (above). If you are comfortable with technical tools, you can also point Beranda at a folder that rclone or Syncthing keeps filled.
radio_hint: Search 50,000+ free stations and add your favourites. The sound plays on the device that shows the screen (your tablet), with a volume slider on the screen. Here, “Play” lets you test the sound on this page.
radio_help: Stations come from Radio Browser, a free, volunteer-run directory with no account and no clicks tracked. Pick one and press Play: the sound comes out of the device showing this page. On the tablet, tap ▶ in the radio box of the main screen; the slider next to it sets the volume. Some stations are offline or only play in their own country: if one does not start, try another. (On an iPhone or iPad the volume buttons on the side control the loudness instead of the slider.)
feed_fail: Could not read this feed ({err}). Check the address.
pin_hint: This page only opens from your home network. A PIN adds one more lock. Leave the box empty to keep things as they are.
saved: Saved. The mirror updates within a minute.
demo_readonly: There is nowhere to save the settings.
preview_hint: Style, mode and language change live; the rest after saving.
forbidden: Open this page from a phone or computer connected to the same Wi-Fi as the mirror.
screen_hint: Turn the picture for a screen hung upright, and switch the screen off at night.
screen_help: Rotation: choose 90° or 270° if the screen hangs upright (portrait), 180° if it is upside down. Night hours: leave both boxes empty to keep the screen on all the time. On the Raspberry Pi the screen itself is switched off, which saves power; on a tablet the page just goes dark.
factory_reset_help: Erases all your settings and puts Beranda back as on its first day. Your photos are kept.
not_installed: Installed by hand: these buttons work only after installing with install.sh (see the README).
requested_update: Updating… the page will come back in a minute or two.
requested_reboot: The Raspberry Pi is restarting. Come back to this page in a minute.
requested_reset: Resetting… Beranda is restarting with its original settings. Reload this page in a few seconds.
tv_hint: Shows what is on TV tonight — from 20:00, for the next 3 hours, in your local time — for the channels you tick. Beranda finds a guide for your country; you only choose the channels.
tv_ok: Found {n} channel(s). Tick the ones to show.
tv_none: No channels yet — paste a guide address above and press “Find channels”.
tv_help: An XMLTV guide is a plain file, published for free by community projects, that lists what is on each channel and when. The buttons above are the usual ones for your country, tested live when you open this page. These projects are run by volunteers and can move or disappear: if none answers, search the web for “XMLTV” plus your country, or see the iptv-org/epg project on GitHub, then paste the address above and press “Find channels”. Tick the channels you watch.
voice_hint: Speak to the screen: tap the microphone button at the bottom right of the main screen, then say a short sentence (“what's the weather”, “play France Inter”, “next station”, “louder”, “stop”). It uses the microphone of the tablet that shows Beranda, not the Raspberry Pi. See below what you can say, and add phrases of your own.
voice_help: How to use it, step by step. 1) Tick “Show the microphone button” and press Save. 2) On the tablet, open Beranda in Chrome or Edge (they turn speech into text using the browser maker's online service, so your voice goes over the internet — Beranda itself keeps nothing). 3) Browsers only allow microphones on “secure” pages, and an address like http://beranda.local:8080 is not secure: on the tablet open chrome://flags/#unsafely-treat-insecure-origin-as-secure, type Beranda's address (for example http://192.168.1.20:8080), set it to Enabled and restart Chrome. 4) Tap the round microphone at the bottom right of the main screen. The first time, Chrome asks permission to use the microphone: tap Allow. 5) Say your sentence. Beranda answers out loud and does it. The tablet listens in the display language you chose in box 2; ten languages have built-in phrases (English, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Brazilian Portuguese, Arabic, Swahili, Indonesian); any other language understands the English phrases, plus your own phrases in any language.
history_hint: A few events that happened today in history, in your language's Wikipedia, so they relate to your part of the world. Fetched once a day; nothing about you is sent besides the date and the language.
photos_dropbox_hint: In Dropbox, share a folder (Share → Create link) and paste the link here. Beranda copies its pictures now, then again every few hours.
photos_save_first: Press Save at the bottom first, then try again.
photos_other_folder_hint: Only for advanced users: a folder on the Pi that another tool (rclone, Syncthing) keeps filled. Leave this empty to use Beranda's own folder.
radio_error: This station does not play. Try another one.
tv_suggest_searching: Looking for a guide for your country…
tv_suggest_found: Free guides found for {country} — tap one:
tv_suggest_none: No free guide answered for {country} right now. You can paste one below (see Help).
voice_check_ok: ✔ This device can use voice control.
voice_check_unsupported: ✖ This browser cannot listen. Use Chrome (or Edge) on the tablet.
voice_check_insecure: ✖ This page is not “secure”, so the browser blocks the microphone. Open Help below to see how to allow it.
photos_bad: not a picture the frame can show (JPG, PNG, WebP or GIF)
photos_err_link: That does not look like a Dropbox shared-folder link. In Dropbox: Share → Create link, then paste it here.
photos_err_big: too big (15 MB per picture, 400 MB for a Dropbox folder)
photos_err_net: Dropbox could not be reached. Check the internet connection and try again.
tv_more: {n} more channels – type a name above to find them
voice_defaults_title: What you can say, out of the box
voice_own_hint: Teach Beranda a phrase of your own: type what you will say, then choose what should happen. Your phrases always win over the built-in ones.
voice_phrase_ph: What you will say, e.g. good night
voice_reply_ph: What Beranda answers, e.g. Sleep well
voice_save_note: After ticking, press Save at the bottom of the page. The microphone button then appears at the bottom right of the main screen within a minute (reload the screen to see it at once).
widgets_hint: Small extras shown on the main screen. Each one can be switched off: untick it and press Save.
w_chart_hint: A curve of the temperature for the next 24 hours, with rain, wind and the nights shaded. It sits next to your photos.
w_air_hint: Small coloured dots: green is fine, yellow to purple means more care. Pollen only shows in Europe, during the pollen season.
w_eph: Name day, length of the day, local calendar
w_eph_hint: The saint of the day (in the countries that have one), how long the day lasts, and the calendar used in your country (Hijri, Chinese lunar, Japanese era…).
w_alerts: Official weather warnings in my area
w_alerts_hint: Shows the weather warnings (wind, storms, heat…) issued by your country's weather service, through the European MeteoAlarm network. Works in about 38 European countries and Israel.
w_area_unsupported: Warnings are not available for this country.
w_area_error: The warning service cannot be reached right now. Try again later.
w_area_calm: No warning for “{area}” right now. That is normal when the weather is calm.
w_area_others: Areas with a warning at this moment: {list}. If yours is among them under another spelling, type it like that.
w_clock2_hint: A small second clock under the date, handy for family or friends abroad. Start typing a city or a zone, such as Asia/Tokyo or America/New_York.
w_clock2_bad: This time zone does not exist. Pick one from the list.
widgets_help: Where the data comes from: Open-Meteo (weather, air quality from the Copernicus CAMS service), MeteoAlarm (warnings) and nameday.abalin.net (name days). All three are free and need no account. If the internet is down, these extras simply disappear for a while.
reset_prompt: To start again from zero, type the word “{word}” below.
city_changed: New town chosen. The region (regional holidays) and the warnings area were reset to match it: check boxes 2 and 4.
limit_reached: Maximum reached: {n} {what} on this device. Remove one to add another.
device_line: Your device: {device} · {mem} GB of memory. Limits adapted to it: “{profile}” profile.
advanced_hint: For people at ease with computers. If in doubt, leave everything here as it is: Beranda works perfectly without touching it.
port_hint: Beranda's address ends with a number after a colon, :8080 by default (for example http://beranda.local:8080/admin). That number is the port. Change it only if another program on the same device already uses 8080.
port_impact_title: What changes when you do this
port_impact_1: The address of the display and of this settings page changes: it ends with your new number instead of :8080. Update your bookmarks and the shortcut on the tablet's home screen.
port_impact_2: Beranda restarts, which takes about ten seconds. A screen plugged into the Pi reloads by itself. A tablet used as the screen has to be pointed to the new address by hand.
port_impact_3: If you use voice control on a tablet, redo the one-time Chrome microphone setting with the new address: the old one no longer counts.
port_impact_4: Your settings, photos and favourites are kept. “Start over from scratch” (just below) brings the port back to 8080.
port_impact_5: If the new port cannot be used when Beranda starts, it goes back to 8080 on its own, so you can never be locked out.
port_range_hint: A number from 1024 to 65535 that nothing else uses, for example 8081 or 8888. Beranda checks that it is free.
port_err_range: Choose a whole number from 1024 to 65535.
port_err_busy: Another program already uses this port. Choose another number.
port_err_same: This is already the port in use.
port_done: Done. Beranda is restarting on the new port. This page opens the new address in a few seconds, or open it now:
port_done_manual: Saved. Beranda was not started by the installer, so restart it yourself for the change to apply (then open {url}).
coffee_hint: Beranda is free. If it brightens your wall, a coffee is always welcome.
port_pending: Saved: {port}, it applies after Beranda restarts.
factory_reset_all: Start over and erase photos and data
factory_reset_all_help: Erases everything: settings, photos and downloaded data. Beranda starts again as new.
reset_all_intro: You are about to erase for good:
reset_all_settings: all your settings (country, language, theme, calendar links, PIN…)
reset_all_data: the downloaded data (weather, news, calendars, TV guide)
reset_all_final_note: This cannot be undone. Beranda then restarts as on its first day.
requested_reset_all: Erasing… Beranda is restarting as new. Reload this page in a few seconds.
area_cleared: The town was changed, so the warnings area (box 4) was emptied: type the area of your new town and press Test.
https_hint: Browsers only give the microphone to “secure” pages. Beranda answers both ways on the same address: just write https:// instead of http://.
https_impact_1: Open the same address with an “s”: https:// instead of http:// (the port number does not change).
https_impact_2: The first time, the browser warns that the connection is “not private”: the certificate is made by Beranda itself. Choose “Advanced”, then “Continue”. Nothing leaves your home network.
https_impact_3: Allow the microphone when the browser asks. The usual http:// address keeps working, and so does the screen on the Pi.
voice_check_tip: Easiest fix: open this same page with https:// instead of http:// (see the Advanced user box).
diag_title: Diagnostic file (to help find a problem)
diag_hint: Download a small text file that describes this Beranda: version, device, your settings, what the display is showing, recent errors and the browser you are using. Send it along with a bug report. It holds no password, calendar link, Dropbox link, feed address or PIN (web addresses are cut to the site name and your place is rounded to about 10 km). Open it in any text editor to check before sharing.
diag_failed: The file could not be made ({err}).
https_here: ✔ You are on the secure address: the microphone is allowed here.
https_unavailable: The secure address is not available on this device (the “openssl” tool is missing: sudo apt install openssl, then restart Beranda).
voice_test: Test the microphone on this device
voice_test_silence: The microphone works but heard nothing. Try again, a little closer.
voice_err_not_allowed: The microphone is blocked for this page. Click the icon on the left of the address bar (padlock or “Not secure”), set Microphone to Allow, then reload the page. Also check that Windows/macOS lets the browser use the microphone.
voice_err_audio_capture: No microphone was found on this device. Plug one in (a headset or a webcam with a microphone), or use the tablet.
voice_err_network: The browser's speech service cannot be reached: it needs the internet (Chrome sends the voice to Google, Edge to Microsoft). Check the connection, or try Google Chrome.
voice_err_service_not_allowed: This browser refuses its speech service on this page. Use Google Chrome, and check that speech services are not turned off in the browser's settings.
voice_err_other: The microphone did not work ({code}). Download the diagnostic file (Advanced user) and send it.
area_mismatch: This area (“{area}”) does not match your town, {town}, whose area is “{suggested}”: no warning would ever show.
area_missing: No area yet. The area of {town} is “{suggested}”.
voice_edge: Microsoft Edge often fails to recognise speech here (its speech service answers “network”): use Google Chrome for voice control.
wifi_hint: The Wi-Fi networks this Pi knows. It joins the best one by itself at every start. Adding a network never cuts the current one.
wifi_hotspot_on: The safety network “Beranda setup” is open right now: no known Wi-Fi was found.
wifi_cable: a network cable is plugged in too
wifi_net_on: safety net on: with no known network for 2 minutes, the Pi opens its own Wi-Fi “Beranda setup”
wifi_add_hint: Search the networks around and tap yours, or type its name (for a hidden network). The Pi remembers it and uses it whenever it is in range.
wifi_none_around: No network found. Move the Pi closer to the box and search again.
wifi_hidden: Hidden network (its name is not broadcast)
wifi_saved_ok: Saved: “{name}”. The Pi uses it whenever it is in range. To use it right now, press “Use now” next to it.
wifi_open_hint: This network has no password: leave the box empty.
wifi_switching: Trying “{name}”… For up to 45 seconds this page may stop answering: that is normal. If it works, find Beranda again at {address} from a phone or computer on that network. If not, the Pi goes back by itself.
wifi_switched: Done: the Pi is now on “{name}”.
wifi_switch_back: “{name}” did not work (password? out of range?). The Pi went back to “{back}”.
wifi_help: Networks are saved by the Pi's own system (NetworkManager), so they stay after a restart, an update, or even without Beranda. Passwords stay there too: never in Beranda's settings, never in the diagnostic file. Several networks can be saved (home, holiday house…): the Pi joins the best one in range. Safety net: if the Pi finds no known network for 2 minutes (new box, changed password), it opens its own Wi-Fi “Beranda setup”. Join it from a phone: a page opens to pick the right network. It closes by itself once the Pi is connected again.
wifi_err_bad_name: Type the name of the network (32 characters at most).
wifi_err_bad_password: A Wi-Fi password has 8 to 63 characters (leave it empty for an open network).
wifi_err_not_saved: The network could not be saved. Check the name and the password.
wifi_err_unknown_network: This network is not saved any more. Reload the page.
wifi_err_in_use: This is the network in use: save and use another one first (or plug in a cable).
wifi_err_not_forgotten: The network could not be forgotten.
wifi_err_switch_failed: That network did not work and the previous one could not be found again. Wait two minutes: the safety net opens “Beranda setup”.
wifi_err_nmcli_missing: This system does not use NetworkManager, so Beranda cannot manage its Wi-Fi.
wifi_err_timeout: No answer from the Pi. Reload the page in a minute.
wifi_err_not_installed: Wi-Fi settings work on a Pi installed with Beranda's installer.
wifi_err_failed: Something went wrong. Download the diagnostic file (Advanced user) and send it.
